convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to load 'ColorXXDPO' custom indicator with multiple smoothing method parameters, and depends on two external .mqh libraries (SmoothAlgorithms.mqh, TradeAlgorithms.mqh) for custom smoothing algorithms and trade execution logic

derived_values.name: min_rates_total - minimum bars needed for indicator warmup
TimeShiftSec - seconds per indicator timeframe bar

other_exits: Oppposite signal closes existing position: uptrend signal closes sell, downtrend signal closes buy

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MarginMode enum: LOT=fixed lot size, FREEMARGIN=fraction of free margin, BALANCE=fraction of balance, LOSSFREEMARGIN=fraction of free margin minus loss, LOSSBALANCE=fraction of balance minus loss. Default LOT mode uses MM=0.1 as fixed lot.

custom_logic_notes: Signal logic: Value[1]<Value[2] means DPO is rising (bar-1 > bar-2 = uptrend). Within uptrend, if Value[0]>Value[1] (current > previous = accelerating uptrend) then BUY open. Uptrend signal also closes SELL positions. Vice versa for downtrend: Value[1]>Value[2] = DPO falling, Value[0]<Value[1] = accelerating downtrend triggers SELL open and BUY close. The SignalBar input (default=1) offsets which bar to read; when SignalBar=0, signals are checked on every tick without new-bar guard. Signal times are calculated as last bar date + TimeShiftSec for trade algorithm timing. BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen and BuyPosClose/SellPosClose are boolean input gates that can disable buy/sell entry or exit independently.
python_conversion_notes: Requires reimplementation of ColorXXDPO custom indicator logic including two smoothing passes (T3 with period 21 then JJMA with period 5 on DPO values). SmoothAlgorithms.mqh contains JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA algorithms - all must be ported. TradeAlgorithms.mqh contains BuyPositionOpen/SellPositionOpen/BuyPositionClose/SellPositionClose functions with MarginMode-based lot sizing - must be ported. The DPO (Detrended Price Oscillator) calculation with double-smoothing is non-trivial. SL/TP values of 1000/2000 pips suggest 5-digit broker pricing but no digit adjustment logic exists in code - raw point values passed directly. Entry is two-condition: first checks trend direction via buffer[1] vs buffer[2], then checks momentum via buffer[0] vs buffer[1].
